introduction: ERC-6944 defines a resolve-mode value that lets an ERC-4804 client resolve a contract's web3:// requests through the ERC-5219 interface. It was proposed by Gavin John and Qi Zhou in April 2023. A contract signals support by implementing IERC5219Resolver, whose resolveMode() function returns the constant bytes32 value "5219"; an ERC-4804 gateway reads it and then uses ERC-5219's request() method. Note: ERC-6944 is a Draft; the specification is still under active development and may change substantially.
designPurpose: ERC-6944 was designed to make ERC-5219 usable as a resolution mode inside ERC-4804's web3:// scheme. An ERC-4804 client needs to know how each contract expects its requests to be resolved, but before this proposal there was no flag for the ERC-5219 request() interface, only the built-in automatic and manual modes. ERC-6944 fills that gap with one pure function, resolveMode(), returning the fixed bytes32 constant "5219". It avoids ERC-165, since a client can check compatibility by calling resolveMode() itself.
commonUsage: ERC-6944 is implemented by contracts that host an on-chain front-end through ERC-5219 and want browsers and gateways to reach it over a web3:// URL. The value is read by web3:// gateway software and by wallets or browser extensions that resolve ERC-4804 addresses on a user's behalf. Because resolveMode() is pure and returns a compile-time constant, implementations typically inherit a small abstract contract that hard-codes the "5219" return value, adding no storage and negligible gas to the host contract.
fn.resolveMode.desc: Returns the ERC-4804 resolve mode of the contract. It is a pure function that must return the constant bytes32 value "5219" (case-insensitive) to signal that requests should be resolved through the ERC-5219 request() interface.
fn.resolveMode.returns.mode: The resolve-mode identifier, fixed to the bytes32 value "5219" for ERC-5219 resolution.
sim.resolveModeWalkthrough.name: Resolve Mode Walkthrough
sim.resolveModeWalkthrough.desc: Follow an ERC-4804 client as it calls resolveMode() and learns to resolve the contract through ERC-5219.
sim.resolveModeWalkthrough.step.call: The web3:// gateway calls resolveMode() on the target contract to learn how its requests should be resolved.
sim.resolveModeWalkthrough.step.resolve: The contract returns the fixed bytes32 constant "5219", identifying itself as an ERC-5219 resolver.
sim.resolveModeWalkthrough.step.serve: Seeing the "5219" mode, the gateway resolves the request through ERC-5219 and serves the response to the browser.
